comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body:
I've changed [`/demos/info.html`](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/3d117815425cbd05105ec0f0192adc0be91931f2/demos/index.html) config to this:

```diff
<script type="module">
  import mermaid from './mermaid.esm.mjs';
  mermaid.initialize({
    theme: 'forest',
    logLevel: 3,
-   securityLevel: 'loose',
+   securityLevel: 'sandbox',
  });
</script>
```

The first would fail, but others would work fine:

![image](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/assets/87622592/b2b003ad-72f7-4dbf-ba58-bf6b85cc9d1c)

Not sure why yet, maybe a variable has been defined after first one, that's why `e2e` testing is failing.

comments.author: nirname
comments.body:
It may be insignificant, but I would rename it Group, because Group is ubiquitous and too abstract. If it is an html element that contains that SVG, it could be SVGParent, if it is <g> inside svg it could be SVGGroup, or even G (yep, one-letter type name). I am afraid Group is too broad

Not necessary to change this, simply asking

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body:
It's should be assignable to return type of `svg.append('g')`, which is the `g` tag inside an `svg`.

I wasn't really sure what to call it. Originally, it was `G`, but I wasn't really sure does that `G` represents until I [searched](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Element/g) and found it's suppose to be `group`.
